quizName: DMV Practice Test #8 25 Questions • Passing Score 19

questions.question: When riding, the best sitting position:

options.text: Requires you to use your arms to hold yourself up.
Lets you reach the controls easily.
Keeps your arms straight when you hold the handgrips.
Keeps your knees away from the gas tank.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lets you reach the controls easily.
questions.explanation: Sit so you can use your arms to steer, not to hold yourself up. Your arms should be slightly bent when holding the handgrips. Keep your knees against the gas tank to stay balanced.

questions.question: Before carrying a passenger in traffic for the first time, you should:

options.text: Practice riding on a quiet road.
Flash your lights so others can see you.
Practice riding on the road shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Practice riding on a quiet road.
questions.explanation: Before carrying a passenger in traffic, practice on a quiet road first. This helps you get used to how your motorcycle handles with the extra weight.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs are rectangular with white background and black letters. You must follow the rules on these signs.

questions.question: A person with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of ______ or higher is legally intoxicated.
questions.explanation: A person age 21 or older with a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher is legally intoxicated. It is illegal and dangerous to ride while intoxicated.

questions.question: Where is the greatest potential for conflict between a motorcycle and other traffic?
questions.explanation: Intersections have the most potential for conflict. Be extra alert where other vehicles may cross in front of you.

questions.question: How can you increase your ability to be seen at an intersection?

options.text: Try to make eye contact with other drivers.
Always ride with your headlight on.
Ride close to vehicles in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always ride with your headlight on.
questions.explanation: Ride with your headlight on. Choose a lane position that lets oncoming traffic see you best. Keep space between you and other vehicles to escape danger if needed.

questions.question: How do headache, cold, and hay fever medications usually affect your body?

options.text: They make you unable to concentrate.

questions.explanation: Most medications for headaches, colds, hay fever, and allergies make you drowsy and can hurt your riding ability. Know how a medication affects you before you ride.

questions.question: When passing parked cars on your right with no oncoming traffic, you should:

options.text: Stay toward the right side of your lane.
Stay toward the left side of your lane.
Use your rearview mirrors more often than usual.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay toward the left side of your lane.
questions.explanation: Stay on the side of your lane away from the parked cars. This protects you from doors opening or people stepping out between cars.

questions.question: Before a ride, you should instruct a passenger to do all of the following, except:

options.text: Sit as far back as possible.
Get on the motorcycle only after the engine is started.
Hold firmly onto your waist, hips, or belt.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sit as far back as possible.
questions.explanation: Tell passengers to wait until the engine starts before getting on. They should sit as close to you as possible without crowding you. They should hold onto passenger handholds or your waist, hips, or belt. Tell them to stay quiet and still.

questions.question: When you ride a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Turn your head and shoulders to look through turns.
Keep your knees away from the gas tank.
Turn just your head and eyes to look through turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn just your head and eyes to look through turns.
questions.explanation: When turning, look where you want to go by turning only your head. Keep your knees against the gas tank for balance. Keep your arms slightly bent when holding the handgrips.

questions.question: A wobble or shaking of the front wheel and handlebars may be caused by:

options.text: Brakes that are not working properly.

questions.explanation: Most wobbles happen because of improper loading, unsuitable accessories, or incorrect tire pressure.

questions.question: When approaching a blind intersection with a stop sign, riders should:

options.text: Stop at the stop sign then proceed through the intersection.
Ignore the stop sign and move forward to get a better look.
Stop at the stop sign, then move forward slowly to see cross traffic better.
Proceed through the intersection without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop at the stop sign, then move forward slowly to see cross traffic better.
questions.explanation: At a blind intersection with a stop sign, first stop where indicated. Then move forward slowly and stop again just before the cross traffic lane. Lean forward and look around buildings, parked cars, or bushes to check for traffic. Keep your front wheel out of the crossroad while you look.

questions.question: A flat front tire is especially hazardous because:

options.text: The front tire provides power for the bike, so you lose acceleration.
The flat tire will shake the bike, making it hard to use the mirrors.
You won't be able to use the brake.

questions.explanation: A flat front tire is especially dangerous because it affects your ability to steer. If your front tire goes flat while riding, safely leave the road as quickly as possible.

questions.question: A skidding rear tire:

options.text: Removes your ability to change direction.
Is only a concern if the front tire is also skidding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Removes your ability to change direction.
questions.explanation: A skidding rear tire is dangerous and can cause a violent crash and serious injury or death. Too much rear brake pressure locks the rear wheel. Once locked, you cannot change direction. Release the brake to regain control.

questions.question: Many over-the-counter drugs:

options.text: Only affect your riding if you drink alcohol while taking the medication.
Have the same effect on everyone.

questions.explanation: Like alcohol, many drugs (including prescription medications, over-the-counter medications, and illegal drugs) have side effects that can impair your ability to ride safely.

questions.question: If you are riding in traffic when a small animal enters your lane, you should:

options.text: Swerve into other lanes to avoid hitting the animal.
Switch lanes as quickly as possible.
Flash your lights to scare the animal.

questions.explanation: Try to avoid hitting an animal safely. In traffic, stay in your lane. Swerving into another lane can cause you to hit another vehicle. Hitting a small animal is safer than hitting another vehicle.

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: To lower the chance of a crash, you should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Be prepared to react to hazards.

questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, be visible to other drivers and let them know your plans through signaling and lane positioning. Keep enough space around you and watch ahead for hazards. Be ready to react. Do not rely on hoping another driver sees you.

questions.question: What may help if your drive chain slips?
questions.explanation: If your chain slips, tightening it may help. If tightening does not fix the problem, replace the chain before riding.

questions.question: If you must brake and swerve to avoid a hazard, you should:

options.text: Either brake then swerve or swerve then brake.
Brake and swerve at the same time.
Choose to either brake or swerve.
Not swerve and only use the front brake to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Either brake then swerve or swerve then brake.
questions.explanation: If you need to brake and swerve to avoid a hazard, do these actions separately. Do not brake while swerving because this may cause your motorcycle to fall over.

questions.question: What is the best protection when riding a motorcycle?

options.text: Keep space between your motorcycle and other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep space between your motorcycle and other vehicles.
questions.explanation: The best way to avoid hitting other vehicles is to keep distance from them. More space gives you more time to react if another driver makes a mistake. Wearing the right gear is also important.

questions.question: After mounting your motorcycle, which should you NOT do?

options.text: Make sure the mirrors are clean.
Make sure the clutch works smoothly.

questions.explanation: After mounting your motorcycle, check that the clutch, throttle, horn, and brakes work. Clean and adjust the mirrors. Make sure the fuel supply valve is open, not closed.

questions.question: Which is NOT a hazard when another vehicle is passing you?
questions.explanation: When being passed, watch out for the passing vehicle's mirrors hitting you. Be aware of wind gusts from the passing vehicle and objects that passengers might throw. Headlights are not a hazard during passing.

questions.question: How many drinks per hour does the body eliminate on average?
questions.explanation: The body eliminates about one drink per hour on average. The time needed varies by person. It is safest to not drive any vehicle after drinking alcohol.

questions.question: What helps other drivers see your motorcycle at an intersection?

options.text: Swerve within your lane to attract attention.

questions.explanation: Use your headlight to be more visible at intersections. Position your motorcycle in the lane where oncoming traffic can see you best. Keep space around your motorcycle so you can steer away if needed.
